summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would provide interim Commonwealth funding for services outside ordinary annual government operations, including capital spending and financial assistance to other levels of government.
Funding would broadly equal seven twelfths of estimated annual appropriations, with larger allocations for selected coronavirus response needs and a $24 billion ministerial advance.
It would begin on 1 July 2020 or royal assent, whichever occurs later, alongside separate supply bills for ordinary services and parliamentary departments.
changes: Responsible ministers could set conditions, amounts and timing for payments to states, territories and local governments.
The bill would set full-year debit limits for general financial assistance and national partnership payments.
Its appropriation authority would end through repeal at the start of 1 July 2023.
summary.affected: Commonwealth entities, the Finance Minister and state, territory and local governments receiving financial assistance are affected.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The three supply bills—Supply Bill (No. 1) 2020‑2021 ($76.3 billion), Supply Bill (No. 2) 2020‑2021 ($6.7 billion), and Supply (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2020‑2021 ($150 million)—were moved to fund government operations for the first seven months of 2020‑21, with the federal budget rescheduled to 6 October 2020 due to coronavirus uncertainty. The bills include advance to the finance minister provisions of $16 billion and $24 billion for urgent expenditure, subject to additional transparency measures.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the supply bills, highlighting an unprecedented advance to the finance minister with new transparency measures requiring a press release for each use and opposition approval via Senator Gallagher for advances over $1 billion, and urged the government to release updated economic and budget forecasts to avoid a 10-month gap.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The speaker argued for the passage of three supply bills appropriating just under $83.2 billion for the first seven months of 2021, emphasising that the funding is interim and includes no new 2020-21 budget measures, only adjustments for COVID-19 and prior decisions.
